Pharma Portfolio: PLC Stage & NBA Analysis

  • Show All Code
  • Hide All Code
  • View Source

Sales value, volume, and growth diagnostics by Product Life Cycle stage

Published

September 2, 2026

Overview

This report analyzes a 5,000-SKU pharma sales-audit dataset through a Product Life Cycle (PLC) lens — every SKU is tagged as Introduction, Growth, Maturity, or Decline — combined with 5-year sales value/volume trends, quarterly momentum, YoY growth, and realized pricing. The goal is a Next Best Action (NBA) style read of where the portfolio’s value is concentrated and which stages are accelerating or eroding.

Show code 
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.ticker import FuncFormatter

CSV_PATH = "Assignment_BA5_Pharma_PLC_NBA_Dataset_cleaned.csv"

STAGE_ORDER = [
    "1_Introduction_New_Launch",
    "2_Growth_Expansion",
    "3_Maturity_Peak_Harvest",
    "4_Decline_Erosion",
]
STAGE_LABELS = ["Introduction", "Growth", "Maturity", "Decline"]
STAGE_COLORS = ["#4C9AFF", "#36B37E", "#FFAB00", "#FF5630"]

YEAR_COLS_VAL = [
    "sales_value_mar22_cr", "sales_value_mar23_cr", "sales_value_mar24_cr",
    "sales_value_mar25_cr", "sales_value_mar26_cr",
]
YEAR_COLS_UNIT = [
    "sales_unit_mar22_k", "sales_unit_mar23_k", "sales_unit_mar24_k",
    "sales_unit_mar25_k", "sales_unit_mar26_k",
]
YEAR_LABELS = ["Mar'22", "Mar'23", "Mar'24", "Mar'25", "Mar'26"]

QUARTER_COLS = [
    "q1_2024_val", "q2_2024_val", "q3_2024_val", "q4_2024_val",
    "q1_2025_val", "q2_2025_val", "q3_2025_val", "q4_2025_val",
]
QUARTER_LABELS = ["Q1'24", "Q2'24", "Q3'24", "Q4'24",
                   "Q1'25", "Q2'25", "Q3'25", "Q4'25"]

plt.rcParams.update({
    "figure.facecolor": "white",
    "axes.facecolor": "white",
    "axes.edgecolor": "#444444",
    "axes.grid": True,
    "grid.alpha": 0.3,
    "font.size": 10.5,
})

df = pd.read_csv(CSV_PATH)
df["inferred_plc_stage"] = pd.Categorical(
    df["inferred_plc_stage"], categories=STAGE_ORDER, ordered=True
)

print(f"{len(df):,} SKUs loaded.")
5,000 SKUs loaded.

Two data quirks handled below: a few SKUs have a near-zero prior-year base, which produces extreme (>1000%) YoY growth outliers — these are clipped to the 1st–99th percentile for plotting only; the underlying data is untouched. Realized price per unit is plotted on a log scale since it spans ₹3.5 to over ₹4 lakh.

1. Portfolio Mix by PLC Stage

How the 5,000 SKUs split across the four life-cycle stages.

Show code 
counts = df["inferred_plc_stage"].value_counts().reindex(STAGE_ORDER)
pct = counts / counts.sum() * 100

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
bars = ax.bar(STAGE_LABELS, counts.values, color=STAGE_COLORS, edgecolor="white")
for bar, c, p in zip(bars, counts.values, pct.values):
    ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, bar.get_height() + 30,
             f"{c:,}\n({p:.1f}%)", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9.5)

ax.set_title("Portfolio Mix by PLC Stage", fontweight="bold")
ax.set_ylabel("Number of SKUs")
ax.set_ylim(0, counts.max() * 1.2)
fig.tight_layout()

2. Sales Value Trend by Stage

Show code 
grp = df.groupby("inferred_plc_stage", observed=True)[YEAR_COLS_VAL].sum().reindex(STAGE_ORDER)

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
for stage, label, color in zip(STAGE_ORDER, STAGE_LABELS, STAGE_COLORS):
    ax.plot(YEAR_LABELS, grp.loc[stage], marker="o", linewidth=2.2, color=color, label=label)

ax.set_title("5-Year Sales Value Trend by PLC Stage", fontweight="bold")
ax.set_ylabel("Total Sales Value (₹ Cr)")
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda x, _: f"{x:,.0f}"))
ax.legend(title="PLC Stage", loc="upper left", frameon=False)
fig.tight_layout()

Maturity carries the largest absolute base, but Growth-stage value is accelerating fastest, and Decline turns down in the final year.

3. Volume Trend by Stage

Show code 
grp = df.groupby("inferred_plc_stage", observed=True)[YEAR_COLS_UNIT].sum().reindex(STAGE_ORDER)

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
for stage, label, color in zip(STAGE_ORDER, STAGE_LABELS, STAGE_COLORS):
    ax.plot(YEAR_LABELS, grp.loc[stage], marker="o", linewidth=2.2, color=color, label=label)

ax.set_title("5-Year Volume Trend by PLC Stage", fontweight="bold")

4. YoY Value Growth Spread by Stage

Show code 
data = df.dropna(subset=["yoy_growth_val_pct"]).copy()
lo, hi = data["yoy_growth_val_pct"].quantile([0.01, 0.99])
data["yoy_clipped"] = data["yoy_growth_val_pct"].clip(lo, hi)
box_data = [data.loc[data["inferred_plc_stage"] == s, "yoy_clipped"] for s in STAGE_ORDER]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 5.5))
bp = ax.boxplot(box_data, labels=STAGE_LABELS, patch_artist=True,
                 showfliers=False, medianprops=dict(color="black", linewidth=1.5))
for patch, color in zip(bp["boxes"], STAGE_COLORS):
    patch.set_facecolor(color)
    patch.set_alpha(0.75)

ax.axhline(0, color="grey", linewidth=1, linestyle="--")
ax.set_title("YoY Sales Value Growth (%) by PLC Stage", fontweight="bold")
ax.set_ylabel("YoY Growth, Value (%)")
fig.tight_layout()

5. Growth Quadrant (NBA Lens)

Volume growth vs. value growth, bubble size = Mar’26 sales value. This is the classic price/volume decomposition view: stages separate cleanly along the diagonal.

Show code 
data = df.dropna(subset=["yoy_growth_val_pct", "yoy_growth_vol_pct"]).copy()
for col in ["yoy_growth_val_pct", "yoy_growth_vol_pct"]:
    lo, hi = data[col].quantile([0.02, 0.98])
    data[col] = data[col].clip(lo, hi)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.5, 6.5))
for stage, label, color in zip(STAGE_ORDER, STAGE_LABELS, STAGE_COLORS):
    sub = data[data["inferred_plc_stage"] == stage]
    sizes = (sub["sales_value_mar26_cr"] / sub["sales_value_mar26_cr"].max()) * 400 + 15
    ax.scatter(sub["yoy_growth_vol_pct"], sub["yoy_growth_val_pct"],
               s=sizes, alpha=0.45, color=color, edgecolor="white",
               linewidth=0.3, label=label)

ax.axhline(0, color="grey", linewidth=1)
ax.axvline(0, color="grey", linewidth=1)
ax.set_title("Growth Quadrant: Volume vs Value Growth\n(bubble size = Mar'26 sales value)",
             fontweight="bold")
ax.set_xlabel("YoY Volume Growth (%)")
ax.set_ylabel("YoY Value Growth (%)")
leg = ax.legend(title="PLC Stage", loc="upper left", frameon=False)
for handle in leg.legend_handles:
    handle.set_sizes([60])
fig.tight_layout()

6. Top Therapy Areas by Sales Value

Show code 
top = (df.groupby("therapy_area")["sales_value_mar26_cr"]
         .sum().sort_values(ascending=True).tail(10))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.5, 6))
bars = ax.barh(top.index, top.values, color="#4C9AFF", edgecolor="white")
for bar, v in zip(bars, top.values):
    ax.text(bar.get_width() + top.max() * 0.01, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height() / 2,
             f"{v:,.0f}", va="center", fontsize=9)

ax.set_title("Top 10 Therapy Areas by Sales Value (Mar'26)", fontweight="bold")
ax.set_xlabel("Sales Value (₹ Cr)")
fig.tight_layout()

7. Realized Price per Unit by Stage

Show code 
data = df.dropna(subset=["realized_price_per_unit_inr"]).copy()
box_data = [data.loc[data["inferred_plc_stage"] == s, "realized_price_per_unit_inr"]
            for s in STAGE_ORDER]

8. Quarterly Momentum

Show code 
totals = df[QUARTER_COLS].sum()

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.5, 5))
ax.plot(QUARTER_LABELS, totals.values, marker="o", linewidth=2.5, color="#6554C0")
ax.fill_between(range(len(QUARTER_LABELS)), totals.values, alpha=0.12, color="#6554C0")
for i, v in enumerate(totals.values):
    ax.text(i, v + totals.max() * 0.01, f"{v:,.0f}", ha="center", fontsize=9)

ax.set_title("Quarterly Sales Value Momentum (Q1'24-Q4'25)", fontweight="bold")
ax.set_ylabel("Total Sales Value (₹ Cr)")
fig.tight_layout()

Key Takeaways

  • Maturity stage carries the largest absolute sales base but the slowest relative growth — the classic “harvest” profile.
  • Growth-stage SKUs are accelerating fastest in value terms and show the steepest quarter-on-quarter momentum.
  • Decline-stage SKUs are volume- and value-negative in lockstep, visible as the lower-left cluster in the growth quadrant.
  • Introduction SKUs start from a zero base and ramp quickly, but still contribute a small share of total portfolio value.

## Overview

This report analyzes a **5,000-SKU pharma sales-audit dataset** through a
Product Life Cycle (PLC) lens — every SKU is tagged as

the portfolio's value is concentrated and which stages are accelerating or
eroding.

```{python}

    "sales_value_mar22_cr", "sales_value_mar23_cr", "sales_value_mar24_cr",
    "sales_value_mar25_cr", "sales_value_mar26_cr",
]
YEAR_COLS_UNIT = [
    "sales_unit_mar22_k", "sales_unit_mar23_k", "sales_unit_mar24_k",
    "sales_unit_mar25_k", "sales_unit_mar26_k",
]

]

df = pd.read_csv(CSV_PATH)
```

## 1. Portfolio Mix by PLC Stage

How the 5,000 SKUs split across the four life-cycle stages.

```{python}
#| label: fig-plc-distribution
#| fig-cap: "SKU count by PLC stage"

counts = df["inferred_plc_stage"].value_counts().reindex(STAGE_ORDER)
pct = counts / counts.sum() * 100

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
bars = ax.bar(STAGE_LABELS, counts.values, color=STAGE_COLORS, edgecolor="white")
for bar, c, p in zip(bars, counts.values, pct.values):
    ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, bar.get_height() + 30,
             f"{c:,}\n({p:.1f}%)", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9.5)

ax.set_title("Portfolio Mix by PLC Stage", fontweight="bold")
ax.set_ylabel("Number of SKUs")
ax.set_ylim(0, counts.max() * 1.2)

```

## 2. Sales Value Trend by Stage

Maturity carries the largest absolute base, but Growth-stage value is

## 4. YoY Value Growth Spread by Stage

```{python}
#| label: fig-yoy-growth-box
#| fig-cap: "YoY sales value growth (%) by PLC stage, 1st-99th pct clipped"

data = df.dropna(subset=["yoy_growth_val_pct"]).copy()
lo, hi = data["yoy_growth_val_pct"].quantile([0.01, 0.99])
data["yoy_clipped"] = data["yoy_growth_val_pct"].clip(lo, hi)
box_data = [data.loc[data["inferred_plc_stage"] == s, "yoy_clipped"] for s in STAGE_ORDER]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 5.5))
bp = ax.boxplot(box_data, labels=STAGE_LABELS, patch_artist=True,
                 showfliers=False, medianprops=dict(color="black", linewidth=1.5))
for patch, color in zip(bp["boxes"], STAGE_COLORS):
    patch.set_facecolor(color)
    patch.set_alpha(0.75)

ax.axhline(0, color="grey", linewidth=1, linestyle="--")
ax.set_title("YoY Sales Value Growth (%) by PLC Stage", fontweight="bold")
ax.set_ylabel("YoY Growth, Value (%)")
fig.tight_layout()
```

## 5. Growth Quadrant (NBA Lens)

Volume growth vs. value growth, bubble size = Mar'26 sales value. This is
the classic price/volume decomposition view: stages separate cleanly
along the diagonal.

```{python}
#| label: fig-growth-quadrant
#| fig-cap: "Volume growth vs value growth by PLC stage"

data = df.dropna(subset=["yoy_growth_val_pct", "yoy_growth_vol_pct"]).copy()
for col in ["yoy_growth_val_pct", "yoy_growth_vol_pct"]:
    lo, hi = data[col].quantile([0.02, 0.98])
    data[col] = data[col].clip(lo, hi)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.5, 6.5))
for stage, label, color in zip(STAGE_ORDER, STAGE_LABELS, STAGE_COLORS):
    sub = data[data["inferred_plc_stage"] == stage]
    sizes = (sub["sales_value_mar26_cr"] / sub["sales_value_mar26_cr"].max()) * 400 + 15
    ax.scatter(sub["yoy_growth_vol_pct"], sub["yoy_growth_val_pct"],
               s=sizes, alpha=0.45, color=color, edgecolor="white",
               linewidth=0.3, label=label)

ax.axhline(0, color="grey", linewidth=1)
ax.axvline(0, color="grey", linewidth=1)
ax.set_title("Growth Quadrant: Volume vs Value Growth\n(bubble size = Mar'26 sales value)",
             fontweight="bold")
ax.set_xlabel("YoY Volume Growth (%)")
ax.set_ylabel("YoY Value Growth (%)")
leg = ax.legend(title="PLC Stage", loc="upper left", frameon=False)
for handle in leg.legend_handles:
    handle.set_sizes([60])
fig.tight_layout()
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Maturity** stage carries the largest absolute sales base but the
  slowest relative growth — the classic "harvest" profile.
- **Growth**-stage SKUs are accelerating fastest in value terms and show
  the steepest quarter-on-quarter momentum.
- **Decline**-stage SKUs are volume- and value-negative in lockstep,
  visible as the lower-left cluster in the growth quadrant.
- **Introduction** SKUs start from a zero base and ramp quickly, but
  still contribute a small share of total portfolio value.
